projectPriority: Prefer direct original-language research and accurately scoped source records over further micro-UI versioning
findings: 1858 Corpus Reformatorum vol.26, printed p357, PDF screenshot page 5, was opened and its Article X main text and variant note34 visually checked.
CR26 labels earlier 1531 quarto princeps as Ed1, a separate 1531 octavo first altered as Ed2, 1540 quarto as Ed3, 1541–42 octavo as Ed4.
1531 Ed1/Ed2 Article X verb group and 1540 Ed3/Ed4 verb group are differentiated in CR26 note34; this is an 1858 critical apparatus not original-book 16th-century leaf.
Zurich official archive lists K-based Lutheran source edition pp43–46, Z-based Reformed edition pp259–267, MBW Texte 3 no825 K + Z divergences and Usteri 1883 Z facsimile.

GHDI edited transcription and K/Z autograph witness do not yet have a completed diplomatic collation; the archive's 7/13/15 differences remain citation-worthy but not all letter-by-letter transcribed.
Unknown Gruber 1540 non-Variata is still held without catalogue item/VD16 number.
limitations: CR26 page is a nineteenth-century edited scholarly source even though the image is an actual printed page; cannot claim 1531/1540 original book autopsy.
Do not overinterpret the Latin verb difference as evidence of one fully settled doctrinal position or universal confessional reception.
CR26 editorial earlier-edition condemnation morphology/spelling was not claimed letter-perfect against surviving early printed copy.
Current public GitHub repository does not provide private preview access controls for research JSON; production host auth remains unverified.
